o1.biggest_strength: It nails all three levers from my data (silent days 3-5, fit finder hidden, refund-first portal) and writes each message in our voice with one button and an honest expected range.
o1.biggest_mistake: Message 2 asking a first-time buyer to 'change it on the result page before we pack' depends on an unproven 'orders can be changed until packed' assumption, which risks a broken promise if the warehouse can't hold orders.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the copy so every line is grade 6-7 and drop or soften the change-before-packing line into a safer 'reply if you need a different size' fallback.

o2.biggest_strength: The fit-check copy is practical and body-positive ('band on the loosest hook', 'comfort beats the number on the tag'), and the hold-out advice is sensible.
o2.biggest_mistake: The swap saving of 'up to £183,800' assumes every extra swap is a £58 order, which inflates the headline number I'd quote to my team.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Ground the swap saving in a realistic per-swap value (as o1 does at 1,300-2,240 kept orders) and make the day-3 message a clear value-add rather than a status update.

reason: Output 1 reads like it was built from my numbers and my customers, ranks the fixes by money, and every message sounds like us with an honest range; Output 2 is strong but the inflated swap saving and slightly thinner insight make it the second choice.
